title: squarespace.get_product
description: Input/output contract for retrieving a single product by id. GET /products/{id} on the commerce base URL (https://api.squarespace.com/1.0/commerce). This is an 8th action, added beyond the 5 originally scoped in connector.yaml plus list_contacts and get_order, once those seven were complete. VERIFICATION STATUS: the product OBJECT SHAPE ($defs.product below) is already CONFIRMED — duplicated verbatim from list-products.schema.json's identical $defs.product, live-verified against a real GET /products response (fixtures/products.json, 4 products, all type PHYSICAL). What is NOT confirmed is this endpoint's own GET-by-id request/response pattern: only GET /products (list_products) has ever been called live against this API — GET /products/{id} has not. Unverified specifically: whether Squarespace exposes this endpoint at all, what it returns for a nonexistent id, and whether the response is wrapped in a top-level key (the way get_contact's GET-by-id turned out to be — `{ contact: {...} }`, a correction from an earlier flat placeholder model) or returned flat (the way create_order's single-order response is, on the same commerce API as this endpoint). This schema models the output as FLAT (`$ref: #/$defs/product` directly, no wrapper) by analogy to create_order's confirmed flat response — but that is an assumption carried over from a sibling endpoint on the same base URL, not a live finding, and get_contact is direct precedent in this project for that kind of assumption turning out wrong. Needs live verification before this action can be trusted in production — see connector.yaml's known_limitations.

input.title: GetProductInput
input.description: Retrieval is by product id, appended to the commerce base as GET /products/{id}. Same structural note as get-order.schema.json: the commerce base URL does not already end in /products, so no segment-doubling concern exists the way it did for get_contact's resolveUrl() dedup — but whether Squarespace's API actually serves this path at all is UNCONFIRMED; it has never been called live.

id.description: Product identifier, e.g. the `id` field on a list_products response (real observed ids look like "6a72f2378d7a8a3a29161789"). No format is enforced beyond non-empty.

output.title: GetProductResult
output.description: UNCONFIRMED whether this response is wrapped in a top-level key or flat — modeled here as flat by analogy to create_order's confirmed response shape on the same commerce API. See this schema's top-level VERIFICATION STATUS.

examples.description: ILLUSTRATIVE, not a live capture through this endpoint — this endpoint has never itself been called. The product object below is the real, confirmed $defs.product shape (verbatim from list-products.schema.json's live-captured example, from fixtures/products.json), shown here under the flat-output assumption this schema currently models. If live testing finds the real response wrapped in a key instead, this example and the output schema both need updating.

attributes.description: Keys correspond to the product's variantAttributes, e.g. { "Size": "Small" }.

image.description: UNVERIFIED when non-null — every variant captured in fixtures/products.json has image: null. Presumably a per-variant override of the product's images[], shape unconfirmed.

product.title: Product

Duplicated verbatim from list-products.schema.json's identical $defs.product. NOT itself confirmed via get_product — see this schema's top-level VERIFICATION STATUS for what specifically remains unverified about this endpoint.

pricing.description: UNVERIFIED when non-null — null on every captured product (all 4 have per-variant pricing instead). Presumably populated for products without variants; shape unconfirmed.

digitalGood.description: UNVERIFIED when non-null — null on every captured product (all 4 are type PHYSICAL). Presumably populated for type: DIGITAL; shape unconfirmed.
